titolo: Why Did Singapore Get Rich But Malaysia Never Did?
descrizione:
In 1965, Malaysia kicked Singapore out of the country. Today, the average Singaporean is about 7 times richer than the average Malaysian. So what happened?

This is the story of a tiny swampy island with no water, no army and no resources and the big country next door that had everything: land, oil, rubber and tin. The answer to why Singapore got rich and Malaysia got stuck is not what most people think.

If Singapore had stayed in Malaysia, would both countries be richer today? Tell me in the comments 👇

trascrizione_inizio: On August 9th, 1965, a country did something no country had ever done before. It kicked out one of its own cities. That city had no fresh water, no army, no oil, no farmland, no natural resources at all. Just a swampy island at the tip of a peninsula with almost 2 million people and nowhere to go. That afternoon, its leader went on live television and in the middle of the press conference, he broke down and cried. The city was Singapore. The country that kicked it out was Malaysia. Today, the average Singaporean produces about $90,000 a year. The average Malaysian, about 12,000. That is more than seven times less. So, how did the country nobody wanted become one of the richest places on Earth? And why did Malaysia, which kept the land, the oil, the rubber, and the tin, fall so far behind? To understand that, we have to go back to a marriage that lasted less [music] than two years. In 1963, Singapore, Malaya, Sabah, and Sarawak joined together to form a new country called Malaysia. On paper, it made perfect sense. Singapore was the port and the trading hub. Malaya had the land and the raw materials. Together, they would be stronger. But, almost immediately, things went wrong. The problem was race. Malaysia was built around the Malay majority with special rights and privileges for Malays written into the system. Singapore was different. Most of its people were Chinese and its leader, Lee Kuan Yew, wanted a Malaysia where everyone was treated equally, no matter their race. To the leaders in Kuala Lumpur, that sounded like a threat. In 1964, racial riots broke out in Singapore. People died and the government in Kuala Lumpur decided the experiment was over. On August 9th, 1965, Singapore was expelled from Malaysia.
